title: Sherpa Tensing — Camp Five: Going to + Infinitive (A2)
description: Camp four kept a rope attached to now. Camp five turns you round to face the ridge above. Going to is the future you can already see from where you stand…

hero.lede: Camp four kept a rope attached to now. Camp five turns you round to face the ridge above. Going to is the future you can already see from where you stand — a plan you've made, or evidence in front of you that makes the next step certain.

cards.head: A plan made in advance
cards.body: You decided before this conversation started.
cards.ex: "We're going to renovate the kitchen in the spring."

cards.head: An intention
cards.body: What you mean to do, whether or not it's arranged.

cards.head: A prediction from evidence
cards.body: Something you can see, hear or feel right now points to it.
cards.ex: "Look at those clouds — it's going to rain."

cards.head: Something on the point of happening
cards.ex: "Careful — that shelf is going to fall."

cards.head: Where things are heading
cards.ex: "At this rate, they're going to miss the deadline."

cards.head: The plan that never happened
cards.body: was / were going to — an intention overtaken by events.
cards.ex: "I was going to call you, but the meeting overran."

cards.head: Affirmative
cards.body: subject + am / is / are + going to + base verb
cards.ex: "She's going to apply." · "They're going to wait."

cards.head: Negative
cards.body: subject + am / is / are + not + going to + base verb

cards.head: Yes / No questions
cards.body: Am / Is / Are + subject + going to + base verb?
cards.ex: "Are you going to accept the offer?"

cards.head: Wh- questions
cards.body: question word + am / is / are + subject + going to + base verb?
cards.ex: "When are you going to tell him?"

charts.head: Conjugation chart
charts.note: Only be changes. Going to never changes, and the verb after it is always the bare infinitive — using "to travel" as the model.

head: Subject
Affirmative
Negative
Question
rows: I am not going to travel (I'm not)
You are not going to travel (aren't)
He is not going to travel (isn't)
She is not going to travel (isn't)
It is not going to travel (isn't)
We are not going to travel (aren't)
They are not going to travel (aren't)

charts.head: The plan that didn't happen: was / were going to
charts.note: Put be into the past and the whole structure becomes an intention that something interrupted. The sentence usually needs a "but".

charts.head: Three mistakes worth naming
charts.note: Almost every error with this structure is one of these three.

head: Not this
This
Why
rows: Be is not optional — it carries the person and the tense.
What follows going to is always the bare infinitive.
Questions invert be. Do has no job here.

charts.note: Both talk about the future. The difference is when the decision was made and what the prediction rests on. Camp seven covers will properly; this is the part you need now.

head: Situation
Going to
Will
rows:
Made before you spoke.
"I'm going to hand in my notice."

Spontaneous — made as you speak.
"Fine — I'll do it myself."

Based on evidence you can point at.
"She's going to win — she's two laps ahead."

Based on opinion or belief.
"I think she'll win."

The natural choice.
"I'll carry that for you."

panels.head: Going to — decided, in motion
items: We are going to leave at dawn.
It 's going to rain — look at that sky.
I 'm going to tell her tonight.

quiz.prompt: Look at those clouds — it _____ rain.
quiz.hint: The evidence is in front of you.
quiz.explain: A prediction based on evidence you can see takes be + going to + base verb: it is going to rain.

quiz.prompt: We _____ the kitchen next spring. (be going to / renovate)
quiz.hint: A plan made well before now.
quiz.explain: The subject is plural, so be is are; and what follows going to is always the bare infinitive: are going to renovate.

quiz.prompt: She _____ apply for the job — she decided last night.
quiz.hint: The decision came before the conversation.
quiz.explain: A decision already made before speaking takes going to. Will would suggest she decided at this moment.

quiz.prompt: He's going to _____ the report tomorrow. (finish)
quiz.explain: Going to is always followed by the bare infinitive: going to finish. Never going to finishing.

quiz.prompt: They _____ wait any longer. (not / be going to)
quiz.explain: The negative is formed on be, not with do: they aren't going to wait.

quiz.prompt: I _____ argue about it. (not / be going to)
quiz.explain: I takes am, and the negative is am not (contracted as I'm not). "Amn't" is not standard English.

quiz.hint: Questions invert be — no auxiliary do.
quiz.explain: Yes/No questions move be in front of the subject: Are you going to tell him?

quiz.hint: Wh- word + be + subject + going to + base verb.
quiz.explain: Wh- questions keep the same inversion: When is she going to announce it?

quiz.prompt: I _____ call you, but the meeting overran.
quiz.explain: Put be into the past and going to describes a plan that never happened: I was going to call you, but…

quiz.prompt: We _____ leave early, but the road was closed.
quiz.explain: We takes were: we were going to leave. The "but" is what tells you the plan failed.

quiz.prompt: "The phone's ringing." "Don't worry — I _____ answer it."
quiz.hint: The decision is being made this second.
quiz.explain: A decision made at the moment of speaking takes will. Going to would mean you had planned to answer the phone before it rang.
Visible evidence, something on the point of happening: you're going to drop that. Will here would sound like a distant prediction.

quiz.prompt: At this rate, the team _____ miss the deadline.
quiz.explain: "The team" is treated as singular here, so it takes is; and the trend in front of you calls for going to.

quiz.prompt: First we're going to check the ropes, then we _____ set off at dawn.
quiz.hint: The second half of one agreed plan.
quiz.explain: Both halves of the plan use the same structure: we're going to check… then we're going to set off. Going to on its own, with no form of be, is the most common error of all.

results: Route set. Every plan and every prediction in the right form.
Solid progress. A couple of loose stones to check before camp six.
Good first attempt. Worth another pass before moving on.
